nodes.summary: For a finite board $B \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, whose cell $(i, j)$ lies in row $i$ and column $j$, the max-rook number of $B$ is the largest size of a subset of $B$ that contains at most one cell of each row and at most one cell of each column, that is, the largest number of non-attacking rooks that can be placed on $B$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $R_k(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ whose max-rook number, the largest number of non-attacking rooks on the Ferrers board, equals $k$.
nodes.title: Partitions with a given max-rook number

nodes.summary: With rows and columns numbered from $0$, the Ferrers board of the partition $(2, 1)$ of $3$ consists of exactly the three cells $(0, 0)$, $(0, 1)$ and $(1, 0)$.
nodes.title: Ferrers board of the partition $(2, 1)$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a partition of $n$, and number rows and columns from $0$. The Ferrers board of $p$ is the finite set of cells $(i, j) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ such that the $(i+1)$-st largest part of $p$ exceeds $j$, that is, such that more than $i$ parts of $p$, counted with multiplicity, exceed $j$.
nodes.title: Ferrers board of a partition

nodes.summary: The function $F$, whose value $F(n)$ for $n \ge 1$ is the largest max-rook number of a partition of $n$, takes the value $F(0) = 1$ at $n = 0$.
nodes.title: The convention $F(0) = 1$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 1$, $F(n)$ is the largest max-rook number $R(\pi)$ over all partitions $\pi$ of $n$, where $R(\pi)$ is the largest number of non-attacking rooks on the Ferrers board of $\pi$. By convention $F(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: Largest max-rook number among partitions of $n$

nodes.summary: The max-rook number $R(\pi)$ of a partition $\pi$ of $n$ is the largest number of non-attacking rooks on the Ferrers board of $\pi$: the largest number of cells of the board, no two in the same row and no two in the same column.
nodes.title: Max-rook number of a partition

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
